title: Global Stocks Hit Longest Losing Run Since 2023: Markets Wrap
byline: SWI swissinfo ch; Bloomberg; Swissinfo API

Global Stocks Hit Longest Losing Run Since 2023: Markets Wrap

(Bloomberg) — A gauge of global stocks is heading for its longest losing streak in three years as the artificial intelligence trade undergoes a sharp unravelling, putting this year’s broader equity gains at risk and roiling metal markets.

The MSCI All Country World Index dropped 0.8% to fall for a seventh day, the longest stretch since September 2023. Pressure on global markets persisted after a strong debut for Anthropic PBC failed to halt the latest leg lower for equities. The Claude chatbot maker dropped more than 6% in early trading on Friday, partly reversing its first day’s 17% gain.

Futures for the S&P 500 fell 0.8%. Those for the Nasdaq 100 retreated 1.7%, with chipmakers poised to extend a 35% slide from their peak in June. A benchmark for Asian equities headed for its worst week since the start of the global pandemic. In Europe, the Stoxx 600 fell 1.7%, with nearly 500 members declining and the technology sector leading losses.

Investors sought safety in bonds. Treasuries rallied across the curve, while German bunds led gains in Europe. The Japanese yen outperformed all its major peers. Copper hit the lowest level since March as the AI selloff fueled worries about global demand. Gold extended its rout, falling below $3,600 an ounce. Brent crude slipped toward $90 a barrel.

“The midterm elections, Nvidia’s strong results and Anthropic’s successful IPO have all failed to serve as clearing events,” said Robert Scholtes at Singular Bank. “Technical selling pressures will likely need to run their course, potentially setting the stage for a short squeeze that could mark a bottom.”

With the S&P 500 on track for its worst month since April 2025, there are few near-term catalysts on the horizon for a rebound. Questions remain over whether the vast spending on the AI buildout can be sustained at a time when borrowing costs look set to rise further.

“Looking ahead, we’re monitoring the Federal Reserve’s 9 December meeting for greater clarity on the US interest rate outlook,” said Pruksa Iamthongthong, head of APAC equities at Aberdeen Investments. “Another important period will be late January and early February, when major US hyperscalers report earnings and provide updated capital expenditure guidance.”

What Bloomberg Strategists Say:

“November is proving to be another brutal month for equities around the world. But the point about the continued selloff is that it is still largely about risk sentiment and not so much a statement on how main street is faring. While the adverse feedback loop from stocks to the real economy is something to be concerned about, this is more about unsustainable, frothy valuations getting a reality check.”

Ven Ram, cross-asset strategist. For the full analysis, click here.

Corporate News:

SpaceX sold $32 billion of bonds to fund its purchase of artificial intelligence chips on Thursday, in a complicated and relatively high-yielding transaction that may serve as a model for a wave of similar financings to come. Nvidia Corp. is being investigated by California officials to determine whether any of its actions resulted in advanced chips or confidential information being improperly obtained by China. DayOne Data Centers Ltd. has put plans for its multibillion-dollar US initial public offering on hold, people familiar with the matter said. Nike Inc. and Formula 1 announced a long-term agreement that will see the swoosh become the car racing circuit’s official uniform and apparel partner. Some of the main moves in markets:
